Tab walks folder picker, track list, deck controls, search, settings, then wraps :: open-pill > folder-list > track-list > seek > previous > play > next > mode-group > search > settings > open-pill > folder-list > track-list
Shift+Tab walks the same order backwards, no trap :: folder-list > open-pill > settings > search > mode-group
a key press turns the ring on
the focus ring (2 px primary and 1 px on-primary) moves with Tab: pixels differ between two focus positions :: 2016 pixels differ, in {"x":57,"y":5,"width":898,"height":140}

a pointer press turns the ring off
Alt+2 then Enter selects the row under the ring, and Enter again plays it (D124) :: ring on "01 Alpha tone", now playing index 30, duration 200 s
playback goes to the private null sink (node id) and nowhere else :: 1 output streams, 1 links, all to node 45; sink node 45
Space toggles play and pause in the track list
Space toggles play and pause in the folder list
Space on the focused Play button presses it once
Ctrl+Shift+1 to 4 pick Repeat, In order, Shuffle folder, Shuffle all :: 1->0 2->1 3->2 4->3
Ctrl+M cycles the mode through all four and wraps :: 1 > 2 > 3 > 0 > 1
Ctrl+Right is the next track and Ctrl+Left the previous :: 30 > 31 > 30
Ctrl+Home restarts the track :: position 0.00 s
Alt+Right seeks +10 s :: position 10.00 s
Alt+Shift+Right seeks +60 s :: position 70.00 s
Alt+Left seeks -10 s :: position 60.00 s
Alt+Shift+Left seeks -60 s :: position 0.00 s
a held Alt+Right keeps seeking (key repeat) :: 190.0 s gained in 0.9 s (each press is 10 s)
a held Alt+Right repeats at the rate and delay the compositor announces, and not at all when repeat is off :: 60.0 s with repeat 5 a second after 400 ms, 10.0 s with repeat off
a focused seek bar moves with Left and Right :: 0.0 > 5.0 > 0.0 s
a focused mode group moves with Left and Right :: 1 > 2 > 1
Alt+Down and Alt+Up show the next and previous folder :: Aaa Tones > Mmm Tones > Zzz Tones > Mmm Tones
Ctrl+Shift+G shows the folder of the playing track :: folder "Aaa Tones"

verdicts.description: launch shows the player page, nothing playing, no ring :: folder "Aaa Tones", app pid 479 in unit music-player-e2e-417-wide

Tab walks folder picker, track list, deck controls, search, settings, then wraps :: open-pill > folder-list > track-list > seek > previous > play > next > mode-group > search > settings > open-pill > folder-list > track-list
Shift+Tab walks the same order backwards, no trap :: folder-list > open-pill > settings > search > mode-group
a key press turns the ring on
the focus ring (2 px primary and 1 px on-primary) moves with Tab: pixels differ between two focus positions :: 2016 pixels differ, in {"x":57,"y":5,"width":898,"height":140}
Alt+1 and Alt+2 focus the folder list and the track list
a pointer press turns the ring off
Alt+2 then Enter selects the row under the ring, and Enter again plays it (D124) :: ring on "01 Alpha tone", now playing index 30, duration 200 s
playback goes to the private null sink (node id) and nowhere else :: 1 output streams, 1 links, all to node 45; sink node 45
Space toggles play and pause in the track list
Space toggles play and pause in the folder list
Space on the focused Play button presses it once
Ctrl+Shift+1 to 4 pick Repeat, In order, Shuffle folder, Shuffle all :: 1->0 2->1 3->2 4->3
Ctrl+M cycles the mode through all four and wraps :: 1 > 2 > 3 > 0 > 1
Ctrl+Right is the next track and Ctrl+Left the previous :: 30 > 31 > 30
Ctrl+Home restarts the track :: position 0.00 s
Alt+Right seeks +10 s :: position 10.00 s
Alt+Shift+Right seeks +60 s :: position 70.00 s
Alt+Left seeks -10 s :: position 60.00 s
Alt+Shift+Left seeks -60 s :: position 0.00 s
a held Alt+Right keeps seeking (key repeat) :: 190.0 s gained in 0.9 s (each press is 10 s)
a held Alt+Right repeats at the rate and delay the compositor announces, and not at all when repeat is off :: 60.0 s with repeat 5 a second after 400 ms, 10.0 s with repeat off
a focused seek bar moves with Left and Right :: 0.0 > 5.0 > 0.0 s
a focused mode group moves with Left and Right :: 1 > 2 > 1
Alt+Down and Alt+Up show the next and previous folder :: Aaa Tones > Mmm Tones > Zzz Tones > Mmm Tones
Ctrl+Shift+G shows the folder of the playing track :: folder "Aaa Tones"
Ctrl+G shows the playing track
Ctrl+O puts the keyboard in the folder list (two-pane layout)
the ring starts on the current folder :: ring on "Aaa Tones"
Down, Up, Home and End move the folder ring :: Home Aaa Tones, Down F, Up Aaa Tones, End Zzz Tones
PageUp and PageDown move the folder ring to the ends of a short list :: PageUp Aaa Tones, PageDown Zzz Tones
a letter jumps to the first folder starting with it :: ring on "Zzz Tones"
Left and Right also move the folder ring :: Zzz Tones > Mmm Tones > Zzz Tones
Enter shows the folder under the ring :: folder "Zzz Tones"
Down, Up, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown move the track ring :: Home "01 Omega tone", Down "99 Trash me", Up "01 Omega tone", End "99 Trash me", PageUp "01 Omega tone", PageDown "99 Trash me"
Enter on a row selects it paused, Enter on the selected row plays it, and the next Enter pauses it (D124) :: index 64 selected paused, then playing, then paused
Ctrl+Shift+C copies the file name of the row under the ring to the clipboard :: clipboard of wayland-2: "99 Trash me.wav"
Ctrl+Shift+E opens the file manager on the folder of the row :: xdg-open /home/runner/temp/agent/depot-complete-ci/desktop-runtime-scratch/run-CDN5O1/library/Zzz Tones
Shift+F10 opens nothing: it is Run in JetBrains and is not used (D114) :: no menu, no page change, no shortcut use
Alt+Enter opens the row menu with its first row highlighted (D114) :: menu_open true, menu_ring 0, 312 px wide
the Menu key opens the row menu with its first row highlighted (D114) :: menu_open true, menu_ring 0, 312 px wide

the access letter D of File details runs that row and closes the menu :: the menu closed after one use of an access letter; /home/runner/work/Monochromatic/Monochromatic/source/package/music-player/desktop-app/target/e2e/shots/wide-access-key-notice.png
in the open track menu Down, Up, Enter and Escape work (menu opened by right click) :: timed out waiting for the track menu opening; last states:

Delete moves the file of the row to the trash (scratch XDG trash), with an Undo message :: moved to /home/runner/temp/agent/depot-complete-ci/desktop-runtime-scratch/run-CDN5O1/wide-xdg/data/Trash/files/99 Trash me.wav
a right click opens the track menu at the pointer (pulled back only to stay inside the window), in the two-pane layout :: timed out waiting for the track menu opening; last states:
the track menu is wider than 280 px, so the longest shortcut hint is not cut at the card edge :: timed out waiting for the track menu opening; last states:

hovering the Search button shows a tooltip that names Ctrl+F :: 9781 pixels changed, in {"x":806,"y":8,"width":284,"height":55}; the text is in /home/runner/work/Monochromatic/Monochromatic/source/package/music-player/desktop-app/target/e2e/shots/wide-tooltip-search.png
Ctrl+F opens Search with the query field focused :: focus search-field
bare keys do nothing as shortcuts in the Search field, and typing works :: timed out waiting for the typed query; last states:
Down and Up move through results, Enter opens one and leaves Search :: timed out waiting for a highlighted result; last states:
Escape leaves Search
typing Björk, かめりあ and Hangul with an emoji puts exactly that text in the Search field :: timed out waiting for the query Björk; last states:

a Search result for another track selects it paused and stops the playing track; the same result again plays it (D127) :: track 64 played; the result selected 32 paused (playing false); the same result played it (playing true)

a row whose file cannot be opened stays the selected row, and the next click on it loads it once it decodes (D128) :: timed out waiting for a click on the selected row playing the repaired file; last states:
two quick Shift taps open Search on the player page
two slow Shift taps (600 ms apart) do nothing
a key between the Shift taps cancels the double tap
Shift held with another key is not a tap

a held Shift with repeats is not a double tap :: a modifier key never repeats on Wayland (the client skips modifiers when it repeats a held key, so holding Shift gives one press and one release, as on a real desktop); the case cannot occur, and the pure detector test covers the sequence
Ctrl+Alt+S opens Settings with the list focused :: focus
Ctrl+F does nothing in Settings
double Shift does nothing in Settings
template field: the first Escape returns to the list row, the second closes Settings; bare keys do nothing in the field :: field "template-field" > "settings-list" (settings-list) > page Player
the player page is back with focus restored for keys

Ctrl held: no badge before 300 ms, badges after, gone on release :: shown at about 316 ms with [search=F, folder-trigger=O, previous=Left, next=Right, mode-cycle=M, deck-title=G]; 1993 pixels differ with badges, 0 after release; badges 0

adding Shift narrows the badges to the Ctrl+Shift chords; releasing Shift brings the Ctrl badges back :: Ctrl [search=F, folder-trigger=O, previous=Left, next=Right, mode-cycle=M, deck-title=G] > Ctrl+Shift [open-folder=O, mode-repeat=1, mode-in-order=2, mode-shuffle-folder=3, mode-shuffle-all=4, deck-folder=G, editor-reset=Backspace]
Alt held shows the seek and focus badges :: [folder-list=1, track-list=2, seek-back=Left, seek-forward=Right]
a quick chord (under 300 ms) never flashes the badges
badges never take pointer input: a click through a shown badge reaches the control beneath :: timed out waiting for Search opening from a click through its badge; last states:
a click on an unselected row selects it paused, and clicks on the selected row play it, then pause it (D124) :: timed out waiting for row A answering the click; last states:

rows.uncaughtFailure: CheckFailureError: timed out waiting for the folder of thirty tracks shown in the track pane
rows.conclusion: The live private PID-limit repair crossed the original thread-creation boundary with no observed PID rejection or OOM and verified cleanup. The wide interaction assertions failed and an uncaught setup assertion censored later configured sessions; this is not a complete or passing desktop suite.

verdicts.description: launch shows the player page, nothing playing, no ring :: folder "Aaa Tones", app pid 481 in unit music-player-e2e-410-wide

Tab walks folder picker, track list, deck controls, search, settings, then wraps :: open-pill > folder-list > track-list > seek > previous > play > next > mode-group > search > settings > open-pill > folder-list > track-list
Shift+Tab walks the same order backwards, no trap :: folder-list > open-pill > settings > search > mode-group
a key press turns the ring on
the focus ring (2 px primary and 1 px on-primary) moves with Tab: pixels differ between two focus positions :: 2016 pixels differ, in {"x":57,"y":5,"width":898,"height":140}
Alt+1 and Alt+2 focus the folder list and the track list
a pointer press turns the ring off
Alt+2 then Enter selects the row under the ring, and Enter again plays it (D124) :: ring on "01 Alpha tone", now playing index 30, duration 200 s
playback goes to the private null sink (node id) and nowhere else :: 1 output streams, 1 links, all to node 45; sink node 45
Space toggles play and pause in the track list
Space toggles play and pause in the folder list
Space on the focused Play button presses it once
Ctrl+Shift+1 to 4 pick Repeat, In order, Shuffle folder, Shuffle all :: 1->0 2->1 3->2 4->3
Ctrl+M cycles the mode through all four and wraps :: 1 > 2 > 3 > 0 > 1
Ctrl+Right is the next track and Ctrl+Left the previous :: 30 > 31 > 30
Ctrl+Home restarts the track :: position 0.00 s
Alt+Right seeks +10 s :: position 10.00 s
Alt+Shift+Right seeks +60 s :: position 70.00 s
Alt+Left seeks -10 s :: position 60.00 s
Alt+Shift+Left seeks -60 s :: position 0.00 s
a held Alt+Right keeps seeking (key repeat) :: 180.0 s gained in 0.9 s (each press is 10 s)
a held Alt+Right repeats at the rate and delay the compositor announces, and not at all when repeat is off :: 60.0 s with repeat 5 a second after 400 ms, 10.0 s with repeat off
a focused seek bar moves with Left and Right :: 0.0 > 5.0 > 0.0 s
a focused mode group moves with Left and Right :: 1 > 2 > 1
Alt+Down and Alt+Up show the next and previous folder :: Aaa Tones > Mmm Tones > Zzz Tones > Mmm Tones
Ctrl+Shift+G shows the folder of the playing track :: folder "Aaa Tones"
Ctrl+G shows the playing track
Ctrl+O puts the keyboard in the folder list (two-pane layout)
the ring starts on the current folder :: ring on "Aaa Tones"
Down, Up, Home and End move the folder ring :: Home Aaa Tones, Down F, Up Aaa Tones, End Zzz Tones
PageUp and PageDown move the folder ring to the ends of a short list :: PageUp Aaa Tones, PageDown Zzz Tones
a letter jumps to the first folder starting with it :: ring on "Zzz Tones"

the Menu key opens the row menu with its first row highlighted (D114) :: menu_open true, menu_ring 0, 312 px wide

template field: the first Escape returns to the list row, the second closes Settings; bare keys do nothing in the field :: field "template-field" > "settings-list" (settings-list) > page Player
the player page is back with focus restored for keys

Ctrl held: no badge before 300 ms, badges after, gone on release :: shown at about 316 ms with [search=F, folder-trigger=O, previous=Left, next=Right, mode-cycle=M, deck-title=G]; 1993 pixels differ with badges, 0 after release; badges 0

adding Shift narrows the badges to the Ctrl+Shift chords; releasing Shift brings the Ctrl badges back :: Ctrl [search=F, folder-trigger=O, previous=Left, next=Right, mode-cycle=M, deck-title=G] > Ctrl+Shift [open-folder=O, mode-repeat=1, mode-in-order=2, mode-shuffle-folder=3, mode-shuffle-all=4, deck-folder=G, editor-reset=Backspace]
Alt held shows the seek and focus badges :: [folder-list=1, track-list=2, seek-back=Left, seek-forward=Right]
a quick chord (under 300 ms) never flashes the badges
badges never take pointer input: a click through a shown badge reaches the control beneath :: timed out waiting for Search opening from a click through its badge; last states:
a click on an unselected row selects it paused, and clicks on the selected row play it, then pause it (D124) :: timed out waiting for row A answering the click; last states:

verdicts.description: launch shows the player page, nothing playing, no ring :: folder "Aaa Tones", app pid 485 in unit music-player-e2e-414-wide

Tab walks folder picker, track list, deck controls, search, settings, then wraps :: open-pill > folder-list > track-list > seek > previous > play > next > mode-group > search > settings > open-pill > folder-list > track-list
Shift+Tab walks the same order backwards, no trap :: folder-list > open-pill > settings > search > mode-group
a key press turns the ring on
the focus ring (2 px primary and 1 px on-primary) moves with Tab: pixels differ between two focus positions :: 2016 pixels differ, in {"x":57,"y":5,"width":898,"height":140}
Alt+1 and Alt+2 focus the folder list and the track list
a pointer press turns the ring off
Alt+2 then Enter selects the row under the ring, and Enter again plays it (D124) :: ring on "01 Alpha tone", now playing index 30, duration 200 s
playback goes to the private null sink (node id) and nowhere else :: 1 output streams, 1 links, all to node 45; sink node 45
Space toggles play and pause in the track list
Space toggles play and pause in the folder list
Space on the focused Play button presses it once
Ctrl+Shift+1 to 4 pick Repeat, In order, Shuffle folder, Shuffle all :: 1->0 2->1 3->2 4->3
Ctrl+M cycles the mode through all four and wraps :: 1 > 2 > 3 > 0 > 1
Ctrl+Right is the next track and Ctrl+Left the previous :: 30 > 31 > 30
Ctrl+Home restarts the track :: position 0.00 s
Alt+Right seeks +10 s :: position 10.00 s
Alt+Shift+Right seeks +60 s :: position 70.00 s
Alt+Left seeks -10 s :: position 60.00 s
Alt+Shift+Left seeks -60 s :: position 0.00 s
a held Alt+Right keeps seeking (key repeat) :: 190.0 s gained in 0.9 s (each press is 10 s)
a held Alt+Right repeats at the rate and delay the compositor announces, and not at all when repeat is off :: 60.0 s with repeat 5 a second after 400 ms, 10.0 s with repeat off
a focused seek bar moves with Left and Right :: 0.0 > 5.0 > 0.0 s
a focused mode group moves with Left and Right :: 1 > 2 > 1
Alt+Down and Alt+Up show the next and previous folder :: Aaa Tones > Mmm Tones > Zzz Tones > Mmm Tones
Ctrl+Shift+G shows the folder of the playing track :: folder "Aaa Tones"
Ctrl+G shows the playing track
Ctrl+O puts the keyboard in the folder list (two-pane layout)
the ring starts on the current folder :: ring on "Aaa Tones"
Down, Up, Home and End move the folder ring :: Home Aaa Tones, Down F, Up Aaa Tones, End Zzz Tones
PageUp and PageDown move the folder ring to the ends of a short list :: PageUp Aaa Tones, PageDown Zzz Tones
a letter jumps to the first folder starting with it :: ring on "Zzz Tones"
Left and Right also move the folder ring :: Zzz Tones > Mmm Tones > Zzz Tones
Enter shows the folder under the ring :: folder "Zzz Tones"
Down, Up, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown move the track ring :: Home "01 Omega tone", Down "99 Trash me", Up "01 Omega tone", End "99 Trash me", PageUp "01 Omega tone", PageDown "99 Trash me"
Enter on a row selects it paused, Enter on the selected row plays it, and the next Enter pauses it (D124) :: index 64 selected paused, then playing, then paused
Ctrl+Shift+C copies the file name of the row under the ring to the clipboard :: clipboard of wayland-2: "99 Trash me.wav"
Ctrl+Shift+E opens the file manager on the folder of the row :: xdg-open /home/runner/temp/agent/depot-complete-ci/desktop-runtime-scratch/run-FLHVhn/library/Zzz Tones
Shift+F10 opens nothing: it is Run in JetBrains and is not used (D114) :: no menu, no page change, no shortcut use
Alt+Enter opens the row menu with its first row highlighted (D114) :: menu_open true, menu_ring 0, 312 px wide
the Menu key opens the row menu with its first row highlighted (D114) :: menu_open true, menu_ring 0, 312 px wide

the access letter D of File details runs that row and closes the menu :: the menu closed after one use of an access letter; /home/runner/work/Monochromatic/Monochromatic/source/package/music-player/desktop-app/target/e2e/shots/wide-access-key-notice.png
in the open track menu Down, Up, Enter and Escape work (menu opened by right click) :: timed out waiting for the track menu opening; last states:

Delete moves the file of the row to the trash (scratch XDG trash), with an Undo message :: moved to /home/runner/temp/agent/depot-complete-ci/desktop-runtime-scratch/run-FLHVhn/wide-xdg/data/Trash/files/99 Trash me.wav
a right click opens the track menu at the pointer (pulled back only to stay inside the window), in the two-pane layout :: timed out waiting for the track menu opening; last states:
the track menu is wider than 280 px, so the longest shortcut hint is not cut at the card edge :: timed out waiting for the track menu opening; last states:

hovering the Search button shows a tooltip that names Ctrl+F :: 9781 pixels changed, in {"x":806,"y":8,"width":284,"height":55}; the text is in /home/runner/work/Monochromatic/Monochromatic/source/package/music-player/desktop-app/target/e2e/shots/wide-tooltip-search.png
Ctrl+F opens Search with the query field focused :: focus search-field
bare keys do nothing as shortcuts in the Search field, and typing works :: timed out waiting for the typed query; last states:
Down and Up move through results, Enter opens one and leaves Search :: timed out waiting for a highlighted result; last states:
Escape leaves Search
typing Björk, かめりあ and Hangul with an emoji puts exactly that text in the Search field :: timed out waiting for the query Björk; last states:

a Search result for another track selects it paused and stops the playing track; the same result again plays it (D127) :: track 64 played; the result selected 32 paused (playing false); the same result played it (playing true)

a row whose file cannot be opened stays the selected row, and the next click on it loads it once it decodes (D128) :: timed out waiting for a click on the selected row playing the repaired file; last states:
two quick Shift taps open Search on the player page
two slow Shift taps (600 ms apart) do nothing
a key between the Shift taps cancels the double tap
Shift held with another key is not a tap

a held Shift with repeats is not a double tap :: a modifier key never repeats on Wayland (the client skips modifiers when it repeats a held key, so holding Shift gives one press and one release, as on a real desktop); the case cannot occur, and the pure detector test covers the sequence
Ctrl+Alt+S opens Settings with the list focused :: focus
Ctrl+F does nothing in Settings
double Shift does nothing in Settings
template field: the first Escape returns to the list row, the second closes Settings; bare keys do nothing in the field :: field "template-field" > "settings-list" (settings-list) > page Player
the player page is back with focus restored for keys

Ctrl held: no badge before 300 ms, badges after, gone on release :: shown at about 314 ms with [search=F, folder-trigger=O, previous=Left, next=Right, mode-cycle=M, deck-title=G]; 1993 pixels differ with badges, 0 after release; badges 0

adding Shift narrows the badges to the Ctrl+Shift chords; releasing Shift brings the Ctrl badges back :: Ctrl [search=F, folder-trigger=O, previous=Left, next=Right, mode-cycle=M, deck-title=G] > Ctrl+Shift [open-folder=O, mode-repeat=1, mode-in-order=2, mode-shuffle-folder=3, mode-shuffle-all=4, deck-folder=G, editor-reset=Backspace]
Alt held shows the seek and focus badges :: [folder-list=1, track-list=2, seek-back=Left, seek-forward=Right]
a quick chord (under 300 ms) never flashes the badges
badges never take pointer input: a click through a shown badge reaches the control beneath :: timed out waiting for Search opening from a click through its badge; last states:
a click on an unselected row selects it paused, and clicks on the selected row play it, then pause it (D124) :: timed out waiting for row A answering the click; last states:

compositorSelection.helpOutput:
Host one GUI client in an isolated nested Wayland session

Usage: monochromatic-nested-wayland-session [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...  Client executable followed by its arguments

Options:
      --socket <PATH>                Enable the Unix-socket control API at PATH
      --size <WIDTHxHEIGHT>          Initial nested-screen size in logical pixels; screenshots are this times --scale [default: 1280x720]
      --scale <SCALE>                Initial output scale, 0.5 to 3 in steps of 1/120 (such as 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2); the scale control command changes it while the child runs [default: 1]
      --color-scheme <SCHEME>        Give the child a private appearance portal without changing the host theme; the color-scheme control command switches it while the child runs [possible values: dark, light]
      --accent-color <RRGGBB>        Give the child a private appearance portal that serves this accent color as six hexadecimal digits; the accent-color control command changes it while the child runs
      --notifications <MODE>         Serve recording notification services on the private bus: none (default), freedesktop, or kde (freedesktop plus Plasma's job view server); the notification and job control commands read them [default: none] [possible values: none, freedesktop, kde]
      --isolate                      Run the hosted app in a resource-controlled systemd scope
      --launcher-log                 Give the child a private session bus and record its taskbar progress; the launcher control commands read the record
      --app-cpu-quota <PERCENT>      App CPU cap under --isolate, as percent of one core
      --app-cpu-weight <WEIGHT>      Relative systemd CPU weight for the isolated app
      --accessibility                Give the child a private AT-SPI accessibility bus that reports accessibility as enabled, and read the tree it publishes with the a11y control command
      --repeat-rate <PER_SECOND>     Key repeat rate announced to the child in repeats per second (0 turns repeat off); the child generates the repeats itself, as on every Wayland compositor [default: 25]
      --repeat-delay <MILLISECONDS>  Wait before a held key starts repeating, announced to the child; the repeat-info control command changes the pair while the child runs [default: 200]
      --headless                     Render with surfaceless EGL on the GPU render node instead of a nested window: no parent display is used or needed and no window appears; the default is the nested window
      --gpu <GPU>                    With --headless, the device that renders: auto (the default: Mesa's default render node, then the other render nodes, then software), software (Mesa's CPU rasterizer), or a render node such as /dev/dri/renderD128; an explicit choice never falls back. Invalid without --headless: the nested window renders on its parent compositor's GPU, which this tool cannot choose
      --list-gpus                    Print the render nodes (with PCI id, kernel driver and Mesa renderer) and the software renderer this host offers to --gpu, name the one auto uses, and exit
  -h, --help                         Print help
  -V, --version                      Print version

The first client command starts child arguments. Use -- to separate parent options.
Example: monochromatic-nested-wayland-session --size 800x600 -- app --help

compositorSelection.helpOutput:
Host one GUI client in an isolated nested Wayland session

Usage: monochromatic-nested-wayland-session [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...  Client executable followed by its arguments

Options:
      --socket <PATH>                Enable the Unix-socket control API at PATH
      --size <WIDTHxHEIGHT>          Initial nested-screen size in logical pixels; screenshots are this times --scale [default: 1280x720]
      --scale <SCALE>                Initial output scale, 0.5 to 3 in steps of 1/120 (such as 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2); the scale control command changes it while the child runs [default: 1]
      --color-scheme <SCHEME>        Give the child a private appearance portal without changing the host theme; the color-scheme control command switches it while the child runs [possible values: dark, light]
      --accent-color <RRGGBB>        Give the child a private appearance portal that serves this accent color as six hexadecimal digits; the accent-color control command changes it while the child runs
      --notifications <MODE>         Serve recording notification services on the private bus: none (default), freedesktop, or kde (freedesktop plus Plasma's job view server); the notification and job control commands read them [default: none] [possible values: none, freedesktop, kde]
      --isolate                      Run the hosted app in a resource-controlled systemd scope
      --launcher-log                 Give the child a private session bus and record its taskbar progress; the launcher control commands read the record
      --app-cpu-quota <PERCENT>      App CPU cap under --isolate, as percent of one core
      --app-cpu-weight <WEIGHT>      Relative systemd CPU weight for the isolated app
      --accessibility                Give the child a private AT-SPI accessibility bus that reports accessibility as enabled, and read the tree it publishes with the a11y control command
      --repeat-rate <PER_SECOND>     Key repeat rate announced to the child in repeats per second (0 turns repeat off); the child generates the repeats itself, as on every Wayland compositor [default: 25]
      --repeat-delay <MILLISECONDS>  Wait before a held key starts repeating, announced to the child; the repeat-info control command changes the pair while the child runs [default: 200]
      --headless                     Render with surfaceless EGL on the GPU render node instead of a nested window: no parent display is used or needed and no window appears; the default is the nested window
      --gpu <GPU>                    With --headless, the device that renders: auto (the default: Mesa's default render node, then the other render nodes, then software), software (Mesa's CPU rasterizer), or a render node such as /dev/dri/renderD128; an explicit choice never falls back. Invalid without --headless: the nested window renders on its parent compositor's GPU, which this tool cannot choose
      --list-gpus                    Print the render nodes (with PCI id, kernel driver and Mesa renderer) and the software renderer this host offers to --gpu, name the one auto uses, and exit
  -h, --help                         Print help
  -V, --version                      Print version

The first client command starts child arguments. Use -- to separate parent options.
Example: monochromatic-nested-wayland-session --size 800x600 -- app --help

in the open track menu Down, Up, Enter and Escape work (menu opened by right click) :: menu_ring null > 0 > 1 > 0; Enter ran row 0; closed (index 64)

issues.body:
## What happened

`@monochromatic-dev/module-translation-repair` began importing
`@monochromatic-dev/cli-markdown-lint`, to run the `semantic-line-breaks` fix over text
the pipeline ships. After that, **every import of the translation-repair package threw
before reaching a line of pipeline code**:

```text
Cannot find native binding. npm has a bug related to optional dependencies
(https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828). Please try `npm i` again after
removing both package-lock.json and node_modules directory.
```

The message names npm and optional dependencies. Both are red herrings, and the message
is emitted by Sätteri's napi loader, not by npm or pnpm.

## What is actually going on

Sätteri is a napi package. Its loader calls `require("@bruits/satteri-<platform>")` and
resolves that relative to wherever the loader's own file sits.

The shared rolldown Node config always bundles `@monochromatic-dev/**` and keeps only
DECLARED dependencies external
(`package/config/rolldown/src/index.node.ts`, `package/config/rolldown/README.md`).
So importing the markdown-lint workspace package inlined its source, its `satteri`
import, and Sätteri's loader, into
`package/module/translation-repair/dist/final/node/`.

That directory is not Sätteri's package directory. Resolution from there walks up and
finds no `@bruits/*` link, because pnpm links those under Sätteri's own location and
nowhere else.

## What it is NOT, with the checks that rule each out

**The bindings are installed.** `node_modules/.pnpm` carries
`@bruits+satteri-linux-x64-gnu@0.9.5` and its siblings for every architecture in
`supportedArchitectures`.

**Sätteri resolves them correctly from its own location.** Two independent checks:
`node package/cli/markdown-lint/dist/final/node/cli.mjs <file>` lints and exits 0, and a
scratch script importing markdown-lint's own `dist` ran the fixer over 64 passages with
no binding error.

**`packageExtensions` does not apply.** It adds dependencies to another package's
manifest so pnpm links them under it, curing the case where a package imports something
it never declared, which under this workspace's strict isolation
(`hoist: false`, `nodeLinker: isolated`) is unresolvable FROM THAT PACKAGE'S OWN
LOCATION. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` carries exactly one such entry, `mitata` reaching for
`@mitata/counters`, and its comment states that shape precisely. This failure has the
opposite shape: nothing is missing from Sätteri's location, the code was copied OUT of
that location by the bundler. Editing Sätteri's manifest changes what pnpm links under
Sätteri, which the inlined copy in `dist/final/node/` never consults.

## Current workaround, which is why this issue exists rather than a closed bug

Declaring the transitive dependency in the consumer:

```jsonc
// package/module/translation-repair/package.json
"satteri": "catalog:",
```

Declared means external, so the bundle emits a runtime import rather than a copy, and
node resolves it from the consuming package's own `node_modules`, where Sätteri sits
beside the `@bruits/*` links its loader needs. Verified by reading the built bundle:

```text
grep 'from"satteri"'                    1 match
grep 'Cannot find native binding'       0 files
grep '@bruits/satteri-[a-z0-9-]*'       0 matches
```

**This works and it is a trap.** Any package that imports markdown-lint must declare a
native dependency it never mentions in its own source, learned only by hitting the
failure. The failure surfaces at import time rather than at build time, so a green build
says nothing about it, and the error text points at npm.

## What this issue asks for

1. **Write the troubleshooting doc for the setup as it stands**, so the next person to
   import markdown-lint recognises the error instead of chasing npm and
   `packageExtensions`. It needs the symptom verbatim, the bundling cause, the three
   negative checks above, and the bundle-reading verification.

2. **Then resolve it properly by migrating to an alternative setup**, so the workaround
   stops being load-bearing.

## Candidate alternatives

Relevant history: `doc/handover/markdown-lint-satteri-benchmark.md` records that Sätteri
was adopted as a PARSER SWAP (variant 2) for speed, replacing
`mdast-util-from-markdown` plus micromark, and that the rule engine kept consuming a
standard `mdast.Root`. The rules are therefore already parser-agnostic, which is what
makes the first option cheap.

**A. Split markdown-lint so the rule core carries no parser.** A core package exporting
rules and a fix driver over an `mdast.Root`, with Sätteri confined to the CLI that reads
files.
Pros: consumers importing rules never touch native code, so the trap disappears at its
source rather than being documented; the CLI keeps the measured speed; matches the
parser-agnostic shape the rules already have.
Cons: a new package and a moved subpath; every consumer of `parse` has to say which
parser it wants; `doc/troubleshooting/satteri-offsets.md` records that Sätteri and
micromark offsets differ, so a core used with either parser needs that pinned by a test.

**B. Carve `@monochromatic-dev/cli-markdown-lint` out of `NODE_ALWAYS_BUNDLE`.**
Pros: smallest change, one list entry; fixes every future consumer at once.
Cons: contradicts the deliberate reason `dist/final/node` exists, recorded in
`package/module/translation-repair/rolldown.node.config.ts`, that the executed thing
should be a FILE rather than an import graph; and it treats one package as special
without a rule saying which others are.

**C. Teach the rolldown config to keep any napi package external automatically**, by
detecting `.node` loaders or an `optionalDependencies` binding set in the closure of
what it is about to bundle.
Pros: cures the class rather than this instance, and needs no consumer to know anything.
Cons: the detection is a heuristic on other people's package shapes, and a wrong answer
either re-breaks the bundle or silently externalises something that should be inlined.

**D. Keep the declaration and document it.**
Pros: nothing to build.
Cons: this is the status quo the issue is filed against.

Ranking: A > C > B > D.

A over C because A removes the native dependency from the consumer's path entirely,
while C only stops it being copied: with C, a consumer still ships a runtime dependency
on a native package it never asked for, and the install has to keep working everywhere
that consumer runs.
C over B because C states a rule the build applies to every package, where B names one
package as special and leaves the next napi dependency to fail the same way.
B over D because B at least makes the failure impossible rather than merely legible.

## Reproduction

```bash
git revert --no-commit <the commit adding "satteri": "catalog:">
mise run //package/module/translation-repair:build
node -e 'import("./package/module/translation-repair/dist/final/node/index.mjs")'
```

## Problem

The prepared Depot CI desktop filesystem contains the required packages, but fresh consumers do not have the user-session services required by the existing desktop E2E harness.

## Evidence and reproduction

- [Run `6w30pv5zds`](https://depot.dev/orgs/l4zncjjbj5/workflows/6w30pv5zds), attempts `x8b3b4xhkb` and `kpwm36f319`, verified all 23 requested installed package versions and ImageMagick in distinct fresh sandboxes.
- `mise run //package/music-player/desktop-app:trial:depot:packages:session` recorded PID 1 as `init` and no session-bus environment.
- `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, starting PipeWire user units, and a minimal `systemd-run --user --wait --pipe true` failed with `Failed to connect to bus: No medium found`.
- `pactl info` failed with `Connection failure: Connection refused`.

## Acceptance

- Establish a supported, disposable fresh-session bootstrap or document an evidence-backed execution-route decision.
- Verify a transient user unit, PipeWire graph, PulseAudio-compatible connection, and clean process shutdown in each fresh consumer.
- Then execute the unchanged desktop interaction suite and retain per-session results.

## Observed boundary

The prepared Depot desktop consumer completes the interaction suite while its decode-priority request falls back to normal priority.
That result does not verify the accepted-priority path.

In [run `p5rp4p0wvp`](https://depot.dev/orgs/l4zncjjbj5/workflows/vhpw3k8m1f?job=n1jkfcsz5c&attempt=zfwxb30f4m),

```text
# music_player::thread_priority
rtkit refused the decode thread priority; keeping normal priority
org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply: Message recipient disconnected from message bus without replying
```

`package/music-player/desktop-app/src/thread_priority.rs:80`
calls `MakeThreadHighPriorityWithPID` with the process ID,
thread ID,
and requested nice value.
Its error branch at line 88 emits the warning and returns false.
The diagnostic says “refused”,
but this observed D-Bus error establishes a disconnected recipient without a reply,
not an explicit policy refusal.

All seven sessions passed,
including private audio routing,
and the consumer verified clean shutdown.
No audio underrun or application failure was observed or attributed to this warning.
The snapshot source is `7b31a6eebec64e193e4165cf7125f781daebf719`;
the consumer wrapper is `36d48d72ef7f17a076c6c7b0181e94b108f3a87e`.
Details are in `doc/audit/depot-prepared-desktop-2026-10-16.md`.

## Acceptance

- Determine which service or connection ended and retain its runtime diagnostics.
- Verify the decoder thread's actual nice level after both accepted and failed requests in disposable fixtures.
- Decide and document whether prepared desktop CI should exercise accepted priority or explicitly cover fallback only.
- Use operation-specific wording when a request fails without an explicit refusal response.
- Keep this result separate from the passing interaction assertions and from the core session-manager work in #997.

The name org.a11y.Bus was not provided by any .service files.

issues.body:
## Observed failure

Run `p9r4xl6n12`, attempt `ltfw0kr3cd`, ran the frozen TOML source
`525d2e09f8168a3bdd7e513e26d4c80b363123e5` through harness `409e6ec10600958a5eba45200944ce25eefe7749`.
The file-enforcer container check completed with failure after `79620.70287899999` milliseconds (#1070).
TOML mutation started at `2026-10-17T04:36:53.885Z`.
The provider canceled the job at `2026-10-17T05:04:22.162Z` because it exceeded 30 minutes.
TOML mutation has no terminal result or retained active log artifact.
Independent file-enforcer mutation never ran.
That unexecuted task has a separate historical source path failure in #1068.

## Diagnosed harness boundary

The generic executor buffers stdout/stderr to a file and awaits each child exit without a per-check deadline.
The container wave defaults to a single worker and sequences independent checks in one job.
The mutation runner permits each container session to last 1800 seconds,
and its campaign can start further sessions and retries.
The outer 30-minute job includes preparation and the preceding container check.
The job timeout skipped artifact upload and the final source immutability proof.
The mutation campaign's internal cause is not established.
Neither an out-of-memory kill nor a mutation-source defect has been proved by this timeout.

## Required behavior

Each selected container or mutation gate must run independently,
retain its exact source command and actual outcome,
and preserve incremental logs, source identity, provider usage, and scoped container diagnostics.
A deadline for one gate must leave independent gates eligible to run.
A source failure remains failed.
A started gate's bounded timeout remains timed out, never passed.
A prerequisite timeout before the selected gate starts must retain that distinction.

## Evidence and replay

`doc/audit/depot-toml-reconciliation-2026-10-17.evidence.json` retains the frozen manifest,
all emitted events, exact diagnostics, artifact digests, and provider intervals.
The captured-trace assertion `mise run reconcile-toml -- --assert-complete` fails on missing terminal evidence.
The canceled attempt consumed `1816904` provider milliseconds at `16x64`;
this failed usage remains in the audit.

## Duplicate search

An all-state GitHub search for TOML mutation timeout found #247 and #479,
which do not describe this executor deadline, evidence-retention, or independent-check scheduling boundary.
Historical #1068 and #1070 remain distinct source failures.
issues.title: TOML CI timeout loses active mutation evidence and censors an independent gate

issues.body:
## Coverage limitation

The desktop E2E suite records `double-shift/repeat` as not injectable
instead of exercising held-Shift repeat behavior through the application input boundary.
The pure detector has repeat tests;
those tests do not establish the UI event adapter's behavior for the same sequence.
This issue tracks the reported coverage limitation,
not an observed application failure or a proven compositor defect.

## Source and execution evidence

- `package/music-player/desktop-e2e/src/wide-double-shift.ts:163`
  calls `recorder.skip` for `double-shift/repeat`.
  Its reason says the Wayland client does not repeat modifier keys
  and refers to pure detector coverage.
- `package/music-player/desktop-e2e/src/scenario-table.unit.test.ts:115`
  expects 117 executable checks and this one skipped check.
- `package/music-player/desktop-app/src/double_shift_tests.rs:95`
  tests `a_held_shift_with_repeats_is_one_press_and_never_a_double_tap`.
  The test at line 101 checks `repeats_inside_a_tap_do_not_add_a_tap`.
- `package/music-player/desktop-app/src/ui_keys.rs:267`
  forwards `key.repeat` into `ShiftInput::ShiftDown` when the received key is Shift.
  This is the consumer boundary not exercised by the skipped E2E sequence.
- Successful [run 38833901553](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/actions/runs/38833901553),
  job `116758578135`,
  revision `93560fbb09cbec0e1ebb871137820dfb71bad813`,
  records this skip at 01:17:27 UTC on 2026-10-16.
  The wide session reports 75 passes,
  zero failures,
  and one not-injectable case.
  All sessions total 117 passes,
  zero failures,
  and the same one not-injectable case.
- The same run's `seek/alt-right-held` and `seek/hold-repeat-count` checks pass.
  The latter observes 60 seconds of seeking with repeat enabled versus 10 seconds with repeat disabled.
  This positive control shows ordinary held-key repeat is exercised;
  it does not establish held-modifier repeat injection.

`doc/audit/depot-desktop-recovery-2026-10-15.evidence.json`
retains the individual outcomes and source-log digest.

## Acceptance criteria

- Establish whether the held-Shift repeat sequence can reach the application's input adapter
  on each supported runtime using deciding source evidence and an appropriate consumer probe.
- For a reachable sequence,
  add a bounded test at the actual input adapter or a supported native event boundary,
  including a positive control that a real double tap opens Search.
- For an unreachable platform sequence,
  document its platform-specific exclusion and the layer that owns defensive repeat handling.
  Do not invent a physical input event solely to turn a skip into a pass.
- Preserve the existing pure detector tests and distinguish unit,
  adapter,
  and interactive coverage in results.
- Keep `117 passed, 0 failed, 1 not injectable` explicit until the classification or coverage changes.
  Do not count this skip as an executed pass.

All-state issue and PR searches found no existing issue for this specific limitation.
#1004 describes the separate chooser failure and merely mentions the old aggregate skip count.
issues.title: Desktop E2E: held-modifier repeat remains outside interactive coverage

sessionLogRetention.conclusion: The original controller writes the summary then removes its scratch base. The post-command collector therefore cannot retain completed session logs. Actual summary and screenshots are retained. A pre-cleanup log archive remains required.

rows.unexecutedSurface: Wide-session checks after the thirty-track folder setup remain blocked by the retained source CheckFailureError. All independent configured session routes have actual outcome evidence.
rows.conclusion: The unfiltered actual consumer reaches every source-selected route. Original folder-setup and chooser failures remain failed. PID/OOM counters and cleanup pass. The historical desktop receipt omits auto-play metadata, and completed temporary session logs were deleted before collection. This is a development control, not a coherent final replay or a passing complete assertion suite.

collection.scope: Read-only collection. Provider intervals require declared resources before pricing. Gate completion needs independent manifest reconciliation.

compositorSelection.helpOutput:
Host one GUI client in an isolated nested Wayland session

Usage: monochromatic-nested-wayland-session [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...  Client executable followed by its arguments

Options:
      --socket <PATH>                Enable the Unix-socket control API at PATH
      --size <WIDTHxHEIGHT>          Initial nested-screen size in logical pixels; screenshots are this times --scale [default: 1280x720]
      --scale <SCALE>                Initial output scale, 0.5 to 3 in steps of 1/120 (such as 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2); the scale control command changes it while the child runs [default: 1]
      --color-scheme <SCHEME>        Give the child a private appearance portal without changing the host theme; the color-scheme control command switches it while the child runs [possible values: dark, light]
      --accent-color <RRGGBB>        Give the child a private appearance portal that serves this accent color as six hexadecimal digits; the accent-color control command changes it while the child runs
      --notifications <MODE>         Serve recording notification services on the private bus: none (default), freedesktop, or kde (freedesktop plus Plasma's job view server); the notification and job control commands read them [default: none] [possible values: none, freedesktop, kde]
      --isolate                      Run the hosted app in a resource-controlled systemd scope
      --launcher-log                 Give the child a private session bus and record its taskbar progress; the launcher control commands read the record
      --app-cpu-quota <PERCENT>      App CPU cap under --isolate, as percent of one core
      --app-cpu-weight <WEIGHT>      Relative systemd CPU weight for the isolated app
      --accessibility                Give the child a private AT-SPI accessibility bus that reports accessibility as enabled, and read the tree it publishes with the a11y control command
      --repeat-rate <PER_SECOND>     Key repeat rate announced to the child in repeats per second (0 turns repeat off); the child generates the repeats itself, as on every Wayland compositor [default: 25]
      --repeat-delay <MILLISECONDS>  Wait before a held key starts repeating, announced to the child; the repeat-info control command changes the pair while the child runs [default: 200]
      --headless                     Render with surfaceless EGL on the GPU render node instead of a nested window: no parent display is used or needed and no window appears; the default is the nested window
      --gpu <GPU>                    With --headless, the device that renders: auto (the default: Mesa's default render node, then the other render nodes, then software), software (Mesa's CPU rasterizer), or a render node such as /dev/dri/renderD128; an explicit choice never falls back. Invalid without --headless: the nested window renders on its parent compositor's GPU, which this tool cannot choose
      --list-gpus                    Print the render nodes (with PCI id, kernel driver and Mesa renderer) and the software renderer this host offers to --gpu, name the one auto uses, and exit
  -h, --help                         Print help
  -V, --version                      Print version

The first client command starts child arguments. Use -- to separate parent options.
Example: monochromatic-nested-wayland-session --size 800x600 -- app --help

name: readonly semantic bridge host evidence

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: ['main']
    paths:
    - 'package/config/oxlint/**'
    - 'package/ownership-markers/foreign-borrowed/**'
    - 'package/oxlint-plugin/no-restricted-syntax/**'
    - 'package/oxlint-plugin/prefer-readonly-parameter-type/**'
    - 'package/oxlint-plugin/shared/**'
    - 'package/test-fixture/oxlint-no-restricted-syntax/**'
    - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
    - '.github/workflows/readonly-semantic-bridge.yml'
  merge_group:
    branches: ['main']
  push:
    branches: ['main']
    paths:
    - 'package/config/oxlint/**'
    - 'package/ownership-markers/foreign-borrowed/**'
    - 'package/oxlint-plugin/no-restricted-syntax/**'
    - 'package/oxlint-plugin/prefer-readonly-parameter-type/**'
    - 'package/oxlint-plugin/shared/**'
    - 'package/test-fixture/oxlint-no-restricted-syntax/**'
    - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
    - '.github/workflows/readonly-semantic-bridge.yml'

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  semantic-bridge:
    name: semantic bridge (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os:
        - ubuntu-latest
        - macos-15
        - windows-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      MISE_AUTO_INSTALL: 'false'
    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd
      with:
        fetch-depth: 1

    - name: Set up mise without repository-wide tool installation
      uses: jdx/mise-action@c2a87611a18de5b3828c5652fe268e992400cb5c
      with:
        # Resolve "latest" through the GitHub releases API, published releases only,
        # one day old like pnpm's minimumReleaseAge. Without it the action installs
        # whatever mise.jdx.dev/VERSION names, which runs ahead of the GitHub release
        # (2025.8.19, 2026.9.3): doc/troubleshooting/mise-action-version-ahead-of-release.md
        minimum_release_age: 1d
        install: false

    - name: Install package tools
      run: mise install node pnpm

    - name: Install workspace dependencies
      run: mise exec node pnpm -- pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

    - name: Build semantic plugin artifact
      run: mise run //package/oxlint-plugin/prefer-readonly-parameter-type:build:js:node

    - name: Verify native bridge lifecycle and platform paths
      run: mise run //package/oxlint-plugin/prefer-readonly-parameter-type:test:semantic-bridge-host

    - name: Verify external consumer artifact
      run: mise run //package/oxlint-plugin/prefer-readonly-parameter-type:test:external-consumer-host

formatterPreparationIncidents.body:
## Observed boundary

The native and desktop provisional case manifests declare an exact changed-file formatting check,
but the prepared final workflows had no consumer bound to that check.
The affected files are package/music-player/truepeak-core/Cargo.toml and
package/music-player/desktop-app/Cargo.toml at their immutable trial source revisions.
No task-count total can establish this gate's execution.

## Implemented correction

Trial harness 6aefa5d651b8754cbd2d330704e5513cc1157650 adds the exact-file adapter in
package/dev-script/task-util/mise.toml and calls it from native.producers wave native-core
and desktop.linux. Terminal verification propagates a retained failed format result.
The source revision, committed manifest bytes, exact selected file, source-locked dprint version,
and source lock identity are checked without editing authored source files.

## Verification and acceptance limit

The actual Mise helper passes 20 control rows, including valid native/desktop fixtures,
unselected-file positive controls, malformed selected input, symlink/scope rejection,
and a removed-source-guard sensitivity control that restores invalid acceptance.
Both source lockfiles remain unchanged.
These are synthetic Cargo fixtures, not authored Cargo formatting results or final provider acceptance.

formatterPreparationIncidents.body:
## Observed boundary

Local Mise 2026.10.0 linux-x64 (2026-10-02) ran mise install dprint@0.61.1
inside the prepared trial harness with MISE_LOCKED=0.
Although the command names dprint, mise.lock changed its Rust entry from nightly-2026-10-13
to nightly-2026-10-17. The before/after SHA256 values are
95704fad9023cea1b8b530d5de696cfbd839f912aba7c0dc2c1c46519ebef733 and
716878be8e23f6ac111c743951b5003743e81d26af0825d1a794311d06b99186.
The tracked diff proves the lock change, not installation of an unrelated compiler.
Only that exact owned diff was restored, then the worktree verified clean.

## Verified repository workaround

The actual mise --no-config install dprint@0.61.1 invocation exits zero in a disposable fixture
and preserves the original lock SHA256. The formatter adapter at trial harness
6aefa5d651b8754cbd2d330704e5513cc1157650 uses --no-config for installation and execution.
Its actual Mise controls exercise the selected files with source dprint configuration
and preserve source lockfiles. The provider bootstrap's Mise 2026.10.9 remains a separate live boundary.

This tracks the repository preparer and its supported local workaround.
No upstream Mise defect or unrelated compiler installation is inferred from this observation.
